# Windows argument receivers

`npm-node.cmd` and `npm-node.ps1` were generated by npm/cmd-shim 8.0.0 from an inert `#!/usr/bin/env node` entrypoint at `node_modules/provider/cli.js`. They are source-pinned inputs, not programs to execute. The supported no-flags template also matches cmd-shim 6.0.3's source. Modified wrappers, extra flags and environment changes must not pass the whole-template check.

`tests/support/windowsCommandLine.ts` implements the receiver's documented Microsoft C startup rules independently from production quoting. Tests feed the real resolver output through node-pty's actual `argsToCommandLine`, using the same preescaped-string handoff as the PTY host. They then model native CRT/WSL direct execution, not just PowerShell literal parsing. POSIX and Linux direct-exec checks also invoke inert native receivers.

The platform test `tests/integration/terminal/windowsNativeArguments.windows.spec.ts` compiles an inert C# receiver into its own temporary directory (no provider or native dependency rebuild). It uses real PowerShell 5.1, PowerShell 7 Legacy/Standard, and ConPTY, checking exact argv, exit code, private transport removal, npm `.cmd`/`.ps1` bypass, stdin, TTY and Ctrl+C. WSL coverage additionally requires `OPENCOVE_TEST_WSL_DISTRO` and Python 3 in that guest; it writes only its own temporary receiver output. No provider CLI runs.

On a Windows host with the repository's Electron-native node-pty, run:

```powershell
$env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE = '1'
$env:OPENCOVE_TEST_WSL_DISTRO = 'Ubuntu'
& .\node_modules\electron\dist\electron.exe .\node_modules\vitest\vitest.mjs run tests/integration/terminal/windowsNativeArguments.windows.spec.ts
```

The tests do not skip a missing required PowerShell version on Windows: install both Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7. On other platforms the five native tests are reported as skipped, never as proof of Windows execution. Test-only PowerShell invocations disable user profiles and set each binder mode before executing the resolver's unchanged launcher.
